tier1: The admin panel is locked, but the password-change endpoint has no CSRF token. Look carefully at the page source — a meta tag claims protection exists. Does it?
tier2: Three attack paths: (1) CSRF the admin password change — no token, no SameSite cookie, just POST to /admin/settings.php?action=change_password. (2) Backup restore takes a .zip filename and passes it to unzip with no sanitization — inject shell metacharacters in the filename itself. (3) Set your display name to a SQL payload; when admin views the user report, your stored value is interpolated directly into a query. The HTML maxlength on the profile form is client-side only.
